ownership.shared: Each shared file owns its universal rules; operating-contract owns authority/evidence, intake owns questions, flow-rules owns F1-F3, output-folder owns exports.
ownership.references: The skill directory containing a reference is its canonical owner. Other skills link to that file; do not copy its detailed rules.
exceptions: Short incomplete-pack fallback safeguards in SKILL.md
Synchronized marked F1-F3 export blocks in project templates

skills/ui-ux-design/references/starter-s.when: 2. Design system first, before any screen or coding handoff. Record a small system: type scale, spacing scale, color roles, radius, elevation, motion, and a short component list. The user's own system or Figma file always wins. Existing app: extract the current system, mark it Observed, and reuse it. Do not replace it. New app: start from the matching starter in [starter-systems.md](references/starter-systems.md), adapt the accent and type to the subject, propose a small system, mark it Proposed, and get the user's OK before screens. Numbers are required for handoff, but they must come from the observed or approved system, never invented. A starter shown to the user and accepted, or delegated with "you decide", counts as approved.

skills/ui-ux-design/references/anti-slop.when: 5. Trace every visible element to the current phase. Read "Default screens to leave out" in [anti-slop-rules.md](references/anti-slop-rules.md) before adding a region. Put later ideas in notes, not UI.

skills/product-design/references/structu.when: 3. **Structure, only when needed.** With several roles, record types or navigation areas, read [structure.md](../product-design/references/structure.md). Hidden navigation is never access control.

skills/build-pack/references/stack-choic.when: 4. **Stack.** Read [stack-choices.md](references/stack-choices.md). Fit the user's coding tool. Give a reason and a switch point for each choice.
